name: missing_status
summary: The response phase ended without a status ever being observed.
trigger: The response reached end of stream while the recorded status was still zero.
grounding: Transport, and it reads like policy, which is why the argument is written down. 'Do not capture a turn whose upstream status you never saw' is a rule any implementation would endorse — but no other implementation can be in this situation. It exists only because ext_proc can deliver a response body before its headers, violating its own message contract; a path that reads the status off a response object always has one. A reason unreachable by construction elsewhere cannot be a shared contract, however sound the rule behind it sounds.
not_expressible: It is a protocol-ordering violation by the surrounding proxy, not a property of the turn.
notes: Treated as a drop rather than assumed successful: implying success from a missing status would put turns of unknown provenance in the log, and this counter is how the contract violation becomes visible at all.
